The paper avoids major conceptual flaws; the proposed "location-semantics correlation" motivation is well-founded, and the experimental design (using unified tuning settings) is robust relative to the baselines.

However, the paper is not without flaws, primarily regarding technical reproducibility and the completeness of the reporting. The mathematical formulation contains ambiguities regarding channel grouping (notation of $x$ vs $x_g$), and there is a likely inconsistency/typo in the LayerNorm implementation (double application), which must be resolved. Furthermore, while the improvements are statistically significant, the absolute gains (0.3% to 0.9%) are modest, and the authors fail to discuss the clinical practicality of these margins or provide standard deviations to quantify variance. The lack of absolute efficiency metrics (e.g., milliseconds per batch, GB of VRAM) weakens the efficiency claim, as does the absence of a limitations section.

Despite these issues, they do not outweigh the substantial empirical evidence of the method's effectiveness and efficiency. The weaknesses are primarily in the domain of clarification, reporting rigor, and modest scope of analysis rather than fundamental errors in the algorithm or experimental validity. The paper makes a solid, positive contribution to the field and would benefit significantly from minor revisions to clarify the math, fix normalization details, and add error bars. Given the strength of the results and the practical value of the efficiency gains, this paper deserves an acceptance rating, leaning towards the higher end due to the efficiency win.
